Three years since release and the Tab key functionality still gets disabled regularly while playing. The fix is simple, but the problem is still completely unacceptable. I repeatedly failed a Minuteman quest that insisted I should speak to an empty room about their problem with raiders. The final confrontation of the Automatron DLC breaks easily, potentially leaving the player in a savegame loop that requires backtracking an hour or more. The stealth system is ludicrous, with enemies literally brushing past you under totally mystifying open/lit conditions.

If you don't mind spending as much time looking up fixes as you might spend looking up gameplay tips for a quality game, this title might be worth an on-sale investment for you. Be warned, though: Bethesda is fine letting players find workarounds in favor of actually doing the heavy lifting of finding a real solution.

This game holds up very well. The Wasteland is an excellent map to explore, the gameplay loop and the gunplay are both well executed, and the atmosphere and quests are generally fun and memorable. The world, as weird and desolate as it is, feels strangely grounded and believable somehow. The recruitable characters are interesting and well-written as well and worth having around.

A few issues hold it back slightly. The main quest sounds great on paper but was not executed very well, largely in regards to the conflict and motivations between the factions. The dialogue trees are awkward and your character doesn't always say what you intend, although that can be fixed with mods. And of course the notorious inescapable radiant quests, which is unfortunate since the Minutemen are my favorite and the settlement system is a great addition to the game.

But despite those flaws, I still enjoy every minute out there and love coming back every now and then. A fun game to play with an okay story but amazing worldbuilding and exploration.

Way before Walton Goggins brought the Ghoul to life (brilliantly) in the series (also brilliant), Fallout was one of my favourite games. Fallout 4 updates and advances familiar mechanics, fixes (and ultimately then replaces) bugs, and compliments everything that made Fallout 3 and Fallout New Vegas exceptional in their own right. It's a testament to the extraordinary work that has gone into this huge RPG shooter that the many (many) minor bugs you will experience do not detract from the joy that you'll have exploring the wastelands and fleeing as fast and as far as possible from Rad Scorpions and Deathclaws whilst you slowly level up and collect bottlecaps for new equipment.
If you like light-hearted RPGs with a first person shooter vibe, a strong choice driven storyline, with luke warm character development - Fallout could be for you.

War, war never changes.
A ridiculous amount of content, an incredible variety of gameplay, side quests that are a true love letter to the RPG genre, and a Wasteland you get so lost in that you end up questioning your own sanity. If you're looking for a story to fully immerse yourself in—navigating the sheer madness of the Commonwealth, the Institute, and the fate of its factions; if you're looking for an escape from reality where you can (not so peacefully) wander through a fully irradiated world alongside Dogmeat or whichever companion you choose, blasting Deathclaws and Super Mutants while Diamond City Radio drops absolute '40s and '50s bangers in the background... Fallout 4 is the exact game for you.

The game gives you total freedom over pretty much everything, and the DLCs are fantastic. The first time I tried it, I bounced right off: 'Nah, I'm not building a shelter just so this guy can have some water.' But after watching the series, I realized I started on the wrong foot. I gave it a second chance, and the vibe completely blew me away. I fully immersed myself in the wasteland and finally understood just how much potential this game brings to the table

For a hardcore fan of the series this might be a little disappointing as FO4 lacks some of the fun aspects of its predecessors. As you might have also read on the other reviews, RPG and decision making elements have been cut down by size. However, when regarded as a game on its own, it absolutely fantastic and brings tons of new features for you to enjoy! Most people argued that the story is shit but dont get fooled, its not actually bad or anything, its just not as good as the story of New Vegas or FO3. When you make downright awesome games for years and then release a new game with some of the previously fun elements missing, the fanbase tends to get overreactive. Bottomline is, FO4 is fun as fuck, but previous games were better. A must buy game, when it is on sale.

I did not like this game very much when it first came out. I didn't like the changes between Fo3 and FoNV, the reduction of the perk and skills system, etc. I had lost the "rpg" qualities which brought me to love Fo3 and Oblivion. But now I ask myself, why did I like Skyrim and not like Fallout 4? Skyrim suffered a similar transition away from traditional rpg elements. Through asking this question, I have found so much to love about this game. While dialogue and the skill/perk system are somewhat lackluster compared to days of old, this game is filled with beautiful environments and plenty of options for replayability. After having exhausted every nook and cranny of skyrim, coming back and making a new character every few months, I think I have found a new game to fill that spot in my gaming time.

You got your RPG fetch quest and backstory stuff, you got the chance to run amok firing wildly into the irradiated air, and you've even got a little Sims action when setting up settlements! Definitely recommend if you're between genres and want a little bit of everything to play with.

I recently upgraded to a new PC and with the show on prime I felt like playing fallout 4 again. 
I purchased the GOTY bundle to fully experience the game only to find out that, sadly, the game has issue with modern architectures. 

Within just a couple of hours I had all sort of bugs. Loading times taking about 2/5 minutes, screen flickers, weird bugs where I suddenly have a black frame around the game.

I'm on 2 TB of SSD, a Geforce 4060TI and I need to waste my time messing with .ini of the game, scrounging the internet to find the community mods that can somewhat fix a game that recently received a "next gen update" to fix well known bugs (the threads about this sort of things were opened YEARS ago).

I can no longer justify these performance issues in a Bethesda game. Since the days of Morrowind's constant crashes, Bethesda has grown into an industry giant. They are far from a small indie company (and frankly, small indie developers care more about their game's performance than Bethesda does).

Bethesda devs, Todd, how can you justify that your players must rely on community mods to make the game playable? Without the community doing your job your games would be almost, if not entirely, unplayable for many.

I'm very disappointed. Shame on you bethesda.

People really need to stop glazing blatantly awful games such as this one. There is no reasonable reason for this game to be as lauded as it is; it comes to the table with no deck and no chips - boring story, copy-paste characters, poor performance, constant technical issues, repetitive gameplay, dysfunctional DLC, just-above mediocre exploration, and it's from a company that has never developed a title without every single one of these issues.

Like every other BGS game, Fallout 4's sole, single, solitary redeeming factor is the modders. If Bethesda is going to thrive solely on its games' communities making the games enjoyable themselves, then they they should just be a company that sells game dev classes and devkits; or just make Roblox for the Creation Engine.

The argument that this isn't an RPG because your character has a backstory is stupid
Fallout 1- A Vault Dweller that is sent to find a water chip for his Vault and save them from a bunch of mutants. They even gave you a TIME LIMIT to get this done.
Fallout 2- A member of a tribe that is a descendant of the guy from the first game who is destined to find a GECK and save their tribe.
Fallout 3- The child of a doctor within a Vault who is forced to leave because their father runs away to work on a project that him and your mother had been working on before she died.
Fallout NV- A simple delivery person who got shot in the head by a dude and now wants to find that man.

(DISCLAIMER)
I have played all of these games so I know what I'm on about.

Listen. I'm not going to bullshit you. This game's main story is a mess and it can run pretty poorly. It's pretty much the opposite of New Vegas: It has a poor story, but an excellent map and environment. If you're going to mod this game, this is a gem. That's where this game really shines. If you don't do anything else, install the unofficial patch and any of the game's numerous fixes.

The DLC is fun. Nuka World is more of the same, in that it's a great map with kind of a shitty story. Far Harbor's quests are a little lacking, but the story and the many directions it can go are wonderful.

Dialogue has been butchered along with the skill system. There are no real choices to make and you are forced into a role by the story, which undermines the roleplaying aspect that Fallout and Bethesda games are all about. The gunplay is better and thats about it.

New Vegas was better.
